_doc: Revert-verify mutants for ticket 21123711 / req 28cd60a7 (the refusal of `exosync quarantine resolve` names the argument that did not match). Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py packages/cli/tests/unit/commands/quarantine-resolve-refusal-21123711.spec.json after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute; committed with a placeholder so a run cannot mutate a neighbouring session's worktree — integration-test-revert-verify §A76). Guards enumerated from `git diff -U0` (§A8). ⛤ The axes live in the EXISTING production-shape suite (exosync-quarantine.test.ts) rather than a new file: its fixture builds a real temp vault with an AssetSpace declaration, a hand-seeded device-local watermark with a pinned conflict and the FakeGitHubRepo transport, and duplicating that would be a worse fixture, not a cleaner one (test-fixture-realism). No sibling `<base>-verify` harness exists ON PURPOSE — the subject is TypeScript driven by jest, which the driver runs through `harness` (hook-matcher-vs-declared-surface §A19). ⛤ Review LOW-4 corrected an earlier caveat here: it named the `matches.length > 1` branch as a guard without a mutant, but that branch is not in the diff AT ALL (0 lines) — it is the SOURCE of the enumeration form, not a claim being made. The real guards of the diff all carry mutants now, including the path predicate (MQ10) and the repo predicate (MQ11). What still has no mutant IN THIS SPEC is the `.conflict.` exclusion the success message cites, because it lives in core — it has its own spec, quarantine-resolve-refusal-21123711.synctypes.spec.json. ⛤ Four anchors were RE-ANCHORED after the round-1 fix-first commit rewrote this chain (§A71: a spec's anchors protrude into the code its own author is editing). The driver caught it loudly — `якорь встречается 0 раз` — which is the correct failure mode; a silent 0 would have read as 'mutant does not differentiate'.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/src/commands/exosync-quarantine.ts

MQ1_old_single_sentence_restored._note: ORCH-required: the replaced assertion must be an AXIS on the new behaviour, not merely a test that stopped failing. Restoring the retracted one-sentence refusal must redden it. ⛤ The first draft of this mutant reproduced the retracted sentence with its nested backticks around `exosync quarantine list`, which the JSON escaping turned into invalid TypeScript — the driver reported BROKEN, and BROKEN is the ABSENCE of a measurement, not a measurement (§A97). The backticks are dropped; what the mutant restores is the single-sentence SHAPE, which is what the axes judge. ⛤ Predicted [Q2, Q3] and MEASURED [Q1, Q2, Q3]: the mutant also replaces the no-conflicts branch, so Q1's assertion on the new wording fails too — a legitimate third consequence, recorded as measured (§A44), not fitted the other way round.

MQ2_state_claim_for_every_input._note: The conjunctive selector collapsed back into one outcome: every input gets the no-conflicts sentence.

MQ3_path_and_repo_outcomes_swapped._note: The two argument-specific outcomes must not be interchangeable: each names a DIFFERENT argument. ⛤ Re-anchored after the fix-first commit of review round 1 rewrote this chain (§A71): the previous anchor (`} else if (byPath.length === 0) {`) no longer exists. ⛤ Predicted [Q2, Q3] and MEASURED [Q3]: Q2 passes no --repo at all, so `repoFilter !== undefined` short-circuits and the mutated conjunct is unreachable for that input. Recorded as measured (§A44).

MQ4_open_paths_not_enumerated._note: Naming the argument without the executable values leaves the caller guessing — the defect #4206 already fixed for `list`.

MQ6_refusal_exit_code_dropped._note: A guard has TWO deliveries (§A31): the exit code and the diagnostic. This mutant covers the first — losing it while editing the text is the quiet way to weaken the command.

MQ7_device_local_note_dropped._note: Half two of the ticket: the backup is named device-local and deletable. The backup itself is untouched — req e85487a7 pins it.
MQ7_device_local_note_dropped.from:
out(
      `     it stays on this device only — '.conflict.' paths are excluded from BOTH sync ` +
MQ7_device_local_note_dropped.to:
if (false as boolean) out(
      `     it stays on this device only — '.conflict.' paths are excluded from BOTH sync ` +

MQ8_backup_no_longer_written._note: The protection of req e85487a7 must stay predicated: if the preserved-backup line stops printing, Q4 must notice — it asserts the file on disk AND the wording together. ⛤ MEASURED red set (review LOW-3): the driver reports [Q4], but the mutation ALSO fails the pre-existing `keep-remote (zero-loss) …` test in the same suite — its name carries no axis token, so `red_re` cannot extract it and the instrument stays silent about it. Recorded here because a silent extra red is exactly what a later reader would mistake for a narrower mutant.

MQ9_no_mounted_assetspace_guard_dropped._note: Review MEDIUM-1: with no mounted AssetSpace the conflict set is empty for an unrelated reason, and 'no open conflicts' is a quantifier over the empty set — formally true, reporting the opposite cause.

MQ10_path_predicate_always_true._note: Review LOW-4: the path predicate is a real guard of this diff and now has its own mutant instead of a prose caveat.

MQ11_repo_predicate_always_true._note: Review LOW-4, second real guard: the repo filter. Dropping it makes the --repo mismatch resolve instead of refusing.
MQ11_repo_predicate_always_true.from: repoFilter === undefined ? byPath : byPath.filter((c) => c.repoKey === repoFilter);
MQ11_repo_predicate_always_true.to: repoFilter === undefined ? byPath : byPath.filter((c) => c.repoKey !== undefined);

MQ12_repo_value_not_named._note: Review LOW-2: the branch about the passed VALUE must name it — BASE did, and dropping it would regress exactly there.
MQ12_repo_value_not_named.from: `"${conflictPath}" is an open conflict, but not in "${repoFilter}" — a repoKey carries ` +
MQ12_repo_value_not_named.to: `"${conflictPath}" is an open conflict, but the --repo you passed does not match — a repoKey carries ` +
